'''Reznikoff of Ledostrov''', also known as the '''Count of Reznikoff''' and later Duke Reznikoff, was the military commander who ended the [[Pentarchy of Ledostrov]] and became the dominant reforming ruler of the post-Pentarchy duchy.

== Rise ==

Reznikoff commanded the [[Southern Defense Force of Ledostrov]] during the late Pentarchy period. When ordered to suppress a minor insurrection, he refused, incorporated rebels into his forces, and marched on [[Novoanov]].

As Uzryta tried to rally loyalists, Duma conspirators and public unrest shattered the Pentarchy. After [[Uzryta of Ledostrov]] was killed, Reznikoff entered Novoanov and was welcomed by many citizens as a restorer of order.

== Reforms ==

Reznikoff declared himself duke, executed remaining Pentarchs, and began institutional reforms. He expanded the [[Duma of Ledostrov]], added loyal military appointees to the upper house, created a popularly elected lower house, and made anti-corruption an explicit ducal duty.

He also used his military credibility to reform the armed forces and modernize the state. The source describes broader economic reforms in 2003-era wording, so this draft treats industrial-development, agricultural-mechanization, and public-welfare reforms as later or post-1994 unless separately confirmed.

== Source Limits ==

The old source calls Reznikoff the "Great Reformer" and describes 2003-era concerns about his age, his granddaughter, and hereditary succession. This 1994-back draft preserves his reform role but leaves the later succession issue for a post-1994 or modern-state pass.
